properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Isle of Palms, SC Expands Single-Use Plastics Ban
properties.description: Isle of Palms City Council expanded plastic bag ban to include straws, stirrers, and foam containers at food/grocery establishments. Passed March 26 to reduce marine litter from single-use plastics.

properties.title: Hallandale Beach Plastic Straw Ordinance
properties.description: Surfrider Broward Chapter successfully passed ordinance banning single-use plastic straws in Hallandale Beach to reduce marine plastic pollution and fossil fuel use. Enforced Jan 1, 2019.

properties.title: Darien Ditching Single-Use Plastic Bags!
properties.description: Surfrider CT helped pass Darien ordinance banning single-use plastic bags and adding paper bag fee. Reduces pollution, saves taxpayer cleanup costs, incentivizes reusables. Passed June 2019, effective Jan 2020-2021.

properties.title: Monterey Plastics Ordinance
properties.description: Coalition effort to ban single-use plastics in Monterey, CA. Passed Dec 2018, effective Earth Day 2019. Bans plastic straws, requires recyclable/compostable containers, prohibits disposable dine-in ware.

properties.title: Banning Intentional Balloon Releases in East Hampton, NY
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Banning Intentional Balloon Releases in East Hampton, NY
properties.description: Ban on intentional balloon releases in East Hampton, NY to protect beaches and marine life. 774 balloons found in cleanups 2017-2018. Law passed Feb 7, 2019 prohibiting balloon releases town-wide.

properties.title: Illegal Seawall Ordered Removed, Owners Fined $1 Million
properties.description: Surfrider supported CA Coastal Commission order to remove illegal seawall at Victoria Beach, Laguna Beach. Owners rebuilt home without permits, losing seawall rights. Removal protects beach from erosion and sea level rise.

properties.title: Straws Upon Request in California
properties.description: California law AB 1884 requires full-service restaurants to provide plastic straws only upon request. Prevents straws from reaching ocean via storm drains, protecting marine life like sea turtles from ingestion harm.

properties.title: Miami Beach Straw Ban Expansion
properties.description: Surfrider Miami Chapter successfully expanded Miami Beach's 2012 beach straw ban to all city beaches, parks, docks, marinas, boat ramps. Includes plastic stirrers. Adopted July 25th to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

properties.title: Addressing Microplastic Pollution in California
properties.description: California legislation (SB 1422 & SB 1263) requires testing microplastics in drinking water and developing a statewide strategy to understand risks and solutions for microplastic pollution in marine environments.

properties.title: Ban Plastic Bags in Stone Harbor, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban Plastic Bags in Stone Harbor, NJ
properties.description: South Jersey Chapter advocates for plastic bag ban in Stone Harbor. Members educate Borough Council on marine pollution. Town passes local ordinance before state law takes effect, protecting coastal waters from plastic waste.

properties.title: Bag Legislation in Asbury Park, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Bag Legislation in Asbury Park, NJ
properties.description: Jersey Shore Chapter advocated for plastic bag ban in Asbury Park using beach cleanup data. City Council passed legislation banning single-use plastic bags with paper bag fees, effective January 1, 2020.

properties.title: Hueneme Beach Saved from Incompatible Toxic Sediment
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Hueneme Beach Saved from Incompatible Toxic Sediment
properties.description: Prevented 30,000 cubic yards of potentially toxic, fine-grained Port of Hueneme dredged sediment from being deposited on Hueneme Beach. Would have caused poor water quality, steep beach profile, harming recreation and surf quality.

properties.title: No Straws for Portland, Maine
properties.description: Campaign to ban single-use plastic straws, stirrers & splash sticks in Portland, Maine. Advocacy led to unanimous city council passage in Oct 2019, with ban effective Jan 2021 to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

properties.title: Stamford Steps it up to Reduce Single-Use Bags!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Stamford Steps it up to Reduce Single-Use Bags!
properties.description: Stamford, CT banned single-use plastic bags & added 10¢ fee on paper bags (Oct 2018, effective Apr 2019). Reduces pollution, saves cleanup costs, incentivizes reusables. Surfrider CT Chapter supported advocacy.

properties.title: St. Petersburg Straw Ordinance
properties.description: Surfrider's Suncoast Chapter advocated for eliminating single-use plastic straws in St. Petersburg, FL to reduce fossil fuel use and marine litter. Ordinance passed Dec 14, 2014 by Mayor and Commissioners.

properties.title: NO on California AB 2921!
properties.description: Surfrider successfully opposed AB 2921, an industry-led voluntary polystyrene recycling program, advocating instead for policies that ban harmful foam and limit single-use plastic pollution at the source in California.

properties.title: Santa Monica Plastics Reduction
properties.description: Santa Monica banned single-use plastics (straws, utensils, containers) for prepared foods in Aug 2018. Surfrider LA rallied support at City Council. Ordinance effective Jan 2019, supports zero waste goal by 2030.

properties.title: Block Offshore Oil Drilling in New York Waters
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Block Offshore Oil Drilling in New York Waters
properties.description: Ban oil drilling in NY state waters and pipelines from federal waters. Protects jobs, economy dependent on clean beaches. Law signed April 29, 2019 by Gov. Cuomo after campaign by Surfrider chapters and partners.

properties.title: Bag Legislation in Avalon, NJ
properties.description: South Jersey Chapter worked with Avalon, NJ to pass local ordinance banning single-use plastic bags, styrofoam, and plastic straws. Legislation introduced July 2018 after activists began advocacy in June.

properties.title: Bag Legislation in Somers Point, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Bag Legislation in Somers Point, NJ
properties.description: South Jersey Chapter urged Somers Point to pass plastic bag ordinance. City passed 5 cent fee on plastic bags in June 2018, with fees going to merchants rather than state, to reduce plastic pollution.

properties.title: Del Mar Expanded Polystyrene Foam Ban
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Del Mar Expanded Polystyrene Foam Ban
properties.description: Ban on EPS foam foodware in Del Mar restaurants, city facilities & events. Surfrider San Diego advocated & provides educational outreach. Ordinance passed Dec 2018, effective June 2019.

properties.title: Ventura EPS Foam Ban
properties.description: Surfrider Ventura's Plastic Free Ventura campaign launched Earth Day 2018 to reduce single-use plastic litter from beach cleanups. Ventura City Council banned EPS foam foodware at restaurants/stores Nov 2020.

properties.title: Kahala Beach Access Preserved!
properties.description: Surfrider Oahu opposed Kahala Resort's permit for commercial activities on public shoreline. BLNR declined permit renewal Sept 14, preserving public beach access in front of resort in Honolulu.

properties.title: Ban Intentional Balloon Releases In Southampton Town, NY
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban Intentional Balloon Releases In Southampton Town, NY
properties.description: Southampton Town banned intentional balloon releases in June 2019. Balloons threaten marine life and cause power outages. Eastern Long Island Chapter shared beach cleanup data with local government.

properties.title: Ban Foam in East Hampton, NY
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban Foam in East Hampton, NY
properties.description: Eastern Long Island Chapter campaign to ban expanded polystyrene foam in East Hampton food establishments. Beach cleanup data from 2017-2018 supported ordinance passed Jan 2019, effective Earth Day 2019.

properties.title: Surfrider Asked to Join Hawaii Cesspool Working Group
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Surfrider Asked to Join Hawaii Cesspool Working Group
properties.description: Surfrider joined Hawaii's Cesspool Working Group to develop plan converting 88,000 cesspools releasing 53M gallons/day untreated sewage into groundwater. Working Group creates conversion plan by 2050, reports due 2019-2020.

properties.title: Prevent Oil and Gas Drilling In Oregon's Ocean
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Prevent Oil and Gas Drilling In Oregon's Ocean
properties.description: Oregon banned oil/gas drilling in state waters (0-3mi) via SB 256 signed March 2019. Blocks infrastructure for offshore drilling. Protects coast tourism, recreation, fishing industries along Oregon coast.

properties.title: Support New Public Access to Miami Beach
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Support New Public Access to Miami Beach
properties.description: Secured 15-foot public beach access pathway in Miami Beach condo development. Working with developers on dune restoration with native plants. Ensures community beach access and lifeguard safety coverage.

properties.title: Ban oil and gas exploration in Florida's state waters!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban oil and gas exploration in Florida's state waters!
properties.description: Amendment 9 prohibits oil/gas drilling in FL state waters (shoreline to 3 miles offshore). Approved Nov 2018 with 69% voter support after Surfrider advocacy through Constitution Revision Commission process.

properties.title: Remove Trash Cans From Shinnecock Inlet Beach
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Remove Trash Cans From Shinnecock Inlet Beach
properties.description: Eastern Long Island Chapter removed overflowing trash cans at Shinnecock Inlet beach that attracted seagulls and illegal dumping, causing more plastic pollution than they prevented. Completed Jan 2018.

properties.title: San Diego Plastics Reduction
properties.description: Ban on polystyrene containers & single-use plastics at San Diego restaurants/retailers to stop ocean plastic pollution. Includes straws/utensils on request only, foam cooler/beach toy ban. Adopted Jan 2019, effective Feb 2019.

properties.title: Stop Obstruction of Miami Beach Public Waterways
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Stop Obstruction of Miami Beach Public Waterways
properties.description: Surfrider Miami Chapter fought private security blocking public access to Miami Marine Stadium Park for kayaking/paddleboarding. Victory: City acknowledged overreach, issued memo clarifying public access rights.

properties.title: Parking Restrictions at Surfrider Beach in Malibu
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Parking Restrictions at Surfrider Beach in Malibu
properties.description: Defeated Malibu's 2-4am parking restrictions at Surfrider Beach/Malibu Pier. California Coastal Commission denied permit, preserving 24/7 coastal access for swimming, surfing, stargazing. Protects public beach rights under Coastal Act.

properties.title: Surfside Beach, SC Plastic Bag Ban
properties.description: Surfside Beach banned single-use plastic bags in 2018. Businesses must provide reusable or recycled paper bags. Ban effective June 1, 2018, covering all businesses and town events to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

properties.title: City of Malibu Plastic Straw and Utensils Ban
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/City of Malibu Plastic Straw and Utensils Ban
properties.description: Malibu banned plastic straws & utensils at restaurants in Feb 2018, effective June 1. Surfrider LA Chapter advocated for this ordinance to reduce plastic pollution found at beach cleanups that harms marine wildlife.

properties.title: Defend Access to the Miami Marine Stadium Lagoon
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Defend Access to the Miami Marine Stadium Lagoon
properties.description: Successfully opposed 49-vessel mooring field at Virginia Key that threatened mangroves, dolphins, marine species & public access for rowing, swimming, paddleboarding. City Commission dropped plan after protests.
properties.category: Marine habitat protection and public access

properties.title: Manhattan Beach Plastic Pollution Reduction Ordinance
properties.description: Manhattan Beach banned single-use plastic straws, utensils, stirrers & polystyrene items at food/retail locations. Ordinance adopted June 2018, enforced Jan 2019. Part of city's 4th plastic reduction measure since 2008.

properties.title: New Beach Access for Miami Beach
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/New Beach Access for Miami Beach
properties.description: Miami Chapter partnered with developers to add public beach access at 5775 Collins Avenue. Supported proposal through letters and testimony at Miami Beach Design Review Board. Approved December 5th, 2017.

properties.title: Stop the LNG Terminal in Coos Bay
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Stop the LNG Terminal in Coos Bay
properties.description: Surfrider Coos Bay Chapter opposed Jordan Cove LNG export facility threatening 400+ waterways and critical estuarine habitat in Coos Bay, Oregon. Project defeated December 2021 after decade-long campaign.

properties.title: Ban the Bag, Greenwich!
properties.description: Greenwich, CT banned single-use plastic bags in March 2018. Local citizens and Surfrider Connecticut Chapter campaigned for the ordinance, which passed 141-54 and took effect September 2018 to reduce plastic waste.

properties.title: Ban Balloon Releases in Asbury Park, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban Balloon Releases in Asbury Park, NJ
properties.description: Jersey Shore Chapter successfully banned intentional balloon releases in Asbury Park, NJ to prevent marine debris. Ordinance passed Sept 2018 after advocacy work alongside plastic bag legislation.

properties.title: Ban Balloon Releases in Long Beach Township, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban Balloon Releases in Long Beach Township, NJ
properties.description: Surfrider Jersey Shore Chapter campaign to ban intentional balloon releases in Long Beach Township, NJ. Balloons pollute beaches daily. Ordinance passed June 5, 2017 with $500 fine for violators.

properties.title: State Agencies Must Consider Environmental Harms Before Approving Use of State Lands
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/State Agencies Must Consider Environmental Harms Before Approving Use of State Lands
properties.description: Surfrider Kaua'i won landmark ruling requiring environmental review before pesticide operations on state lands 400ft from ocean. Protects West Kaua'i coastline from chemical runoff, drift impacts to beaches, cultural sites.

properties.title: Banning Balloon Releases in North Wildwood, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Banning Balloon Releases in North Wildwood, NJ
properties.description: South Jersey Chapter campaign to ban intentional balloon releases in North Wildwood, Cape May County. Latex/Mylar balloons and plastic ribbons threaten marine environment. First such ordinance in county.

properties.title: Stop New Fossil Fuel Development in the Tacoma Tideflats
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Stop New Fossil Fuel Development in the Tacoma Tideflats
properties.description: Coalition campaign to maintain moratorium on new fossil fuel facilities in Tacoma Tideflats. City Council passed interim regulations Nov 2017 blocking development until sub-area plan finalized, protecting Commencement Bay waters.

properties.title: Beach Access Victory at Kahala Beach
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Beach Access Victory at Kahala Beach
properties.description: Surfrider's Oahu Chapter successfully opposed Kahala Hotel's easement request that would have limited public beach access on Honolulu's South Shore, protecting community rights to pristine shoreline.

properties.title: Plan Calls for Managed Retreat and Restoration of Ocean Beach
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Plan Calls for Managed Retreat and Restoration of Ocean Beach
properties.description: Restoring Ocean Beach SF through managed retreat & beach nourishment. Removes hard armoring exacerbating erosion south of Sloat Blvd. LUP amendment approved May 2018 after 3 decades of advocacy for wider beach access.

properties.title: Say NO to a ban on plastic bag bans in Rhode Island!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Say NO to a ban on plastic bag bans in Rhode Island!
properties.description: Campaign to defeat H5946 bill that would ban local plastic bag bans in RI. Surfrider RI Chapter & partners successfully opposed plastics industry attempt to rescind municipal ordinances & protect local rights to address plastic pollution.

properties.title: Trump Administration Withdraws Southeast Waters from Offshore Drilling
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Trump Administration Withdraws Southeast Waters from Offshore Drilling
properties.description: 10-year moratorium on offshore drilling in FL, GA, SC, NC waters. Surfrider advocates for permanent congressional ban to protect marine ecosystems and coastal economies from oil/gas development and seismic blasting.

properties.title: Protect New England Coral Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Protect New England Coral Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument!
properties.description: Campaign to restore protections for Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument. Biden restored protections Oct 2021, prohibiting commercial fishing to protect unique underwater ecosystems, coral canyons, seamounts in New England.

properties.title: Banning Intentional Balloon Release in Bradley Beach, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Banning Intentional Balloon Release in Bradley Beach, NJ
properties.description: Jersey Shore Chapter successfully advocated for Bradley Beach ordinance 2017-26 banning intentional balloon releases to protect marine environment. $500 fine for violations. Passed October 10, 2017.

properties.title: Phasing Out Atlantic Salmon Net Pens in Washington
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Phasing Out Atlantic Salmon Net Pens in Washington
properties.description: Washington banned open-water Atlantic salmon aquaculture in Salish Sea after net pen collapse released invasive fish. Protects wild Pacific salmon, improves water quality, preserves public trust waters and wave resources.

properties.title: Save the Wave at Surfside Jetty!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Save the Wave at Surfside Jetty!
properties.description: Surfrider advocated for Alternative 1 in Navy's Seal Beach Ammunition Pier reconstruction to protect Surfside Jetty surf break. Navy selected this alternative, preserving the regionally-significant wave spot from destruction.

properties.title: Marine Sanctuaries Protected from Potential Oil and Gas Development
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Marine Sanctuaries Protected from Potential Oil and Gas Development
properties.description: Surfrider Foundation defended CA marine sanctuaries from oil/gas development. Generated 100k comments opposing Trump admin review. Biden terminated review Jan 2021, protecting Channel Islands, Monterey Bay, Cordell Bank, Farallones.

properties.title: Stop Bad Beach Access Bill
properties.description: Campaign to stop HB 735 blocking local governments from protecting public beach access via customary use ordinances in Florida. Bill threatened Walton County's beach access protections. Successfully defeated in 2017.

properties.title: Protected Public Coastal Recreational Access in MI
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Protected Public Coastal Recreational Access in MI
properties.description: Legal campaign supporting broad interpretation of Michigan's Recreation Land Use Act in Otto v. Inn at Watervale case, enabling private landowners to allow public beach and water access for recreation.

properties.title: Prevent dumping of Humboldt Bay dredge spoils on Samoa Beach
properties.description: Surfrider opposed City of Eureka & Harbor District's plan to dump 200,000 cubic yards of dredge spoils on Samoa Beach, impeding public access. EPA rejected the plan in 2017 - Victory!

properties.title: St. Augustine Beach Single Use Plastics Ordinance
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/St. Augustine Beach Single Use Plastics Ordiance
properties.description: Campaign to ban plastic straws, bags, and styrofoam in St. Augustine Beach to prevent marine pollution. Ordinance passed July 1, 2019, making it one of first Northeast Florida cities to eliminate single-use plastics.

properties.title: Clean Border Water Now Lawsuit Settlement
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Clean Border Water Now Lawsuit Settlement
properties.description: Surfrider's Clean Water Act lawsuit settlement addresses decades-long pollution at US-Mexico border. Aims to reduce 75% of contaminated flows, cut beach closures 95% in summer via infrastructure improvements and monitoring.

properties.title: Save Capistrano Beach
properties.description: Replace emergency armoring with nature-based adaptation at Capistrano Beach. North Reach pilot approved Nov 2022. South Reach has 7-year riprap permit. Goal: expand nature-based solutions coastwide.

properties.title: Coral Gables Bag Ban
properties.description: First Florida city to ban single-use plastic bags in May 2017. Addresses marine litter, clogged drains, recycling damage. Surfrider Miami Chapter collaborated with city and businesses to pass ordinance.

properties.title: Support federal Save Our Seas Act to address plastic pollution
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Support federal Save Our Seas Act to address plastic pollution
properties.description: Federal legislation funding NOAA Marine Debris Program for single-use plastics & fishing gear removal, authorizing $10M/year through 2022. Enables severe marine debris event declarations for cleanup after tsunamis & weather events.

properties.title: Dana Point Outdoor Smoking Ban
properties.description: Ordinance prohibiting smoking in all public places in Dana Point to reduce cigarette butt litter in urban and beach areas, preventing plastic filters and toxins from entering waterways and ocean.
properties.funder: Surfrider Foundation South Orange County Chapter

properties.title: Mount Pleasant, SC Bans Single Use Plastic Bags, Containers
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Mount Pleasant, SC Bans Single Use Plastic Bags, Containers
properties.description: Surfrider Charleston eliminated single-use plastic bags & polystyrene foam in Mount Pleasant, SC to protect coastal waters from plastic pollution. Achieved April 2018 through town collaboration.

properties.title: Stopped SC Bill that would Preempt Local Government from Regulating Bags, Containers
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Stopped SC Bill that would Preempt Local Government from Regulating Bags, Containers
properties.description: Defeated H 3529 in SC General Assembly to preserve local authority to regulate bags, containers & packaging that pollute waterways. Charleston & Grand Strand Chapters led opposition, postponing bill in 2017.

properties.title: California Ocean Litter Strategy Adopted
properties.description: CA Ocean Protection Council adopted 2018 Ocean Litter Prevention Strategy to guide 6 years of litter reduction along CA coast, focusing on land-based sources, microplastics, and beach cleanup data coordination.

properties.title: No Balloon Releases in Ventnor, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/No Balloon Releases in Ventnor, NJ
properties.description: Surfrider South Jersey Chapter secured unanimous ban on balloon releases in Ventnor, NJ (Feb 2017) to protect marine animals and birds from entanglement/ingestion. Activists presented ordinance at town meetings.

properties.title: Mallows Bay-Potomac River National Marine Sanctuary
properties.description: Surfrider DC & Ocean City chapters helped approve first National Marine Sanctuary in 20 years, 40 miles south of DC. Protects shipwrecks, cultural heritage. Designated by NOAA 2019 for conservation, education, tourism.

properties.title: No Balloon Releases in Atlantic City, NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/No Balloon Releases in Atlantic City, NJ
properties.description: Atlantic City banned balloon releases in Feb 2017 to prevent marine litter. Balloons entangle wildlife and are ingested by marine animals. Surfrider South Jersey chapter advocated for ordinance across coastal towns.

properties.title: No Pay to Play Ordinance in York!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/No Pay to Play Ordinance in York!
properties.description: Surfrider Maine stopped York's 2016 fee proposal for paddlecraft access to York River. Advocated free public access, first-come policy vs $86 commercial fees. Board scrapped ordinance, will gather data before future proposals.

properties.title: California Legislature Establishes Fund, Authorizes Funding, for Martins Beach Easement
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/California Legislature Establishes Fund, Authorizes Funding, for Martins Beach Easement
properties.description: CA legislature authorized $1M fund to acquire public access easement to Martins Beach. State Lands Commission can allocate funds from Land Bank Fund subaccount to restore permanent coastal access.

properties.title: Fund Florida Water Quality Monitoring
properties.description: Restore funding for Florida Healthy Beaches Program to monitor coastal water quality for fecal bacteria. State cuts in 2011 reduced testing frequency. Victory in 2019 with $500k restoration. Protects beachgoers from contamination.

properties.title: Enforce Hollywood Beach Single-Use Plastic Ordinance
properties.description: Campaign to enforce existing ordinance banning single-use plastics east of Intracoastal Waterway in Hollywood Beach, FL. Protects sea turtles, manatees, dolphins from plastic pollution. Victory: enforcement began Oct 2018.

properties.title: Stop Venoco Offshore Oil Drilling Expansion
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Stop Venoco Offshore Oil Drilling Expansion
properties.description: Campaign to stop Venoco's proposed expansion of Platform Holly oil drilling in California state waters off Goleta. Successfully ended when Venoco quitclaimed leases in April 2018, leading to platform decommissioning.

properties.title: Banning Balloons in Longport, NJ
properties.description: South Jersey Chapter campaign to ban balloon releases in Longport, NJ using Margate's model ordinance. Activists worked with Borough Council to protect marine life from balloon pollution. Ordinance passed in 2016.

properties.title: Laguna Beach Smoking Ban
properties.description: Expanded smoking ban passed May 2017 in Laguna Beach, CA to reduce cigarette litter. Covers beaches, parks, sidewalks, bike paths citywide. Cigarette butts are 1 in 5 items in beach cleanups.

properties.title: Bag Legislation in Ventnor, NJ
properties.description: South Jersey Chapter campaign for single-use bag ordinance in Ventnor, NJ. Conducted cleanups, merchant education from 2015-2018. Resulted in 5-cent fee on paper and plastic bags passed February 2018.

properties.title: Protected the Atlantic from Offshore Oil Drilling
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Protected the Atlantic from Offshore Oil Drilling
properties.description: Permanent withdrawal of Atlantic & Arctic waters from oil/gas drilling announced Dec 2016. Grassroots campaign with 120+ local resolutions, 1000+ business signatures protected critical coastal habitats & economies from drilling risks.

properties.title: Maui Foam Ban
properties.description: Ban polystyrene foam food containers on Maui. Coalition worked with County Council, Ocean Friendly Restaurants program. Polystyrene is top 10 littered item, <1% recycled. Maui first in Hawaii to pass ban.

properties.title: Big Island Foam Ban
properties.description: Surfrider's Hilo & Kona Chapters led coalition to ban EPS foam food containers on Big Island. 7000+ petition signatures, Ocean Friendly Restaurants support. Bill 13 passed Sept 20, part of effort to make Hawaii first foam-free state.

properties.title: Hawaii Dept. of Health Improves Public Notification of Water Quality Issues
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Hawaii Dept. of Health Improves Public Notification of Water Quality Issues
properties.description: Surfrider collaborated with Hawaii DOH to improve water quality public notification. Created website with data, maps, and updates for chronically polluted sites. Started 2016, launched after 1.5 years of stakeholder meetings.

properties.title: Hawaii Passes Ban on all Cesspools and Extends Tax Credit for Replacements
properties.description: Ban on new cesspools in Hawaii to protect groundwater and ocean from 55M gallons daily raw sewage. Gov. Ige signed rule changes Mar 2016. Tax credits support upgrades to septic systems near water sources.

properties.title: Care For The Cove
properties.description: Ensuring US Army Corps of Engineers follows 1998 settlement for sand replenishment at Half Moon Bay, Westport WA. Addresses erosion, safety concerns, and beach recreation impacts from jetty/groin construction since 2013.

properties.title: Protecting Our Coral Reefs & Banning Oxybenzone
properties.description: Hawaii banned sunscreens with oxybenzone & octinoxate to protect coral reefs from toxic chemicals causing DNA damage, bleaching & deformities. Surfrider Hawaii advocated since 2016. Law effective Jan 1, 2021 statewide.

properties.title: Stopped the NY/NJ Williams Gas Pipeline
properties.description: Stopped 23.4-mile fracked gas pipeline across Raritan Bay from Old Bridge NJ to Rockaway Point NY. Opposed due to impacts on water quality, marine habitat, and coastal recreation. Permits denied 2019.

properties.title: Keep South Beach Safe
properties.description: Resolve conflict between jet ski use and surfers at South Beach, Del Norte County through enforcement of CA laws protecting bathers from motorized watercraft within 200 feet of beach.

properties.title: Ban the Bag, Boston!
properties.description: Boston campaign to ban single-use plastic bags under 3ml and charge $0.05 for other bags. Passed unanimously 12-0 by City Council 11/29/17, signed into law by Mayor Walsh to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

properties.title: Public Access Victory in Malibu - First Civil Penalty from California Coastal Commission
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Public Access Victory in Malibu - First Civil Penalty from California Coastal Commission
properties.description: CA Coastal Commission fined property owner $4.185M for blocking public beach access in Malibu for 9 years. First use of civil penalty authority. Supreme Court upheld ruling in 2021, setting precedent for access enforcement.

properties.title: Butts off Miami Beach
properties.description: Installing 200 cigarette butt receptacles throughout Miami Beach to reduce beach litter. Partnership between Surfrider Miami Chapter and City of Miami Beach, funded by $10k city grant. Monitoring effectiveness since 2019.

properties.title: Culver City Polystyrene Foodware Ban
properties.description: Ban on polystyrene foam & rigid plastic foodware at restaurants to reduce Santa Monica Bay pollution. Adopted May 2017, effective Nov 2017. Prevents wildlife consumption of non-biodegradable plastic pieces.

properties.title: Require Access Equity at Mavericks Surf Contest
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Require Access Equity at Mavericks Surf Contest
properties.description: Campaign demanding gender equity at Mavericks surf contest per CA Coastal Act Section 30210. Advocates for multi-heat women's division, equal pay, and access equity beyond physical barriers at Half Moon Bay.

properties.title: Cherry Point Aquatic Reserve Expansion
properties.description: Expanded Puget Sound reserve by 45 acres, protecting herring/eelgrass habitat vital to salmon. Prevented coal terminal development. Surfrider organized cleanups and advocacy. Lummi treaty rights cited. DNR management plan now protects site.

properties.title: Malibu Expanded Polystyrene Ban
properties.description: Surfrider advocated for Malibu to expand its EPS foam ban, prohibiting sale/use of foam food service ware, coolers, packing materials, and maritime products. Adopted November, creating one of strongest US EPS policies.

properties.title: Keep Beaches Protected in Puerto Rico
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Keep Beaches Protected in Puerto Rico
properties.description: Defeated Senate Bill 1621 to prevent legalization of private development encroachment on public beaches in southern Puerto Rico, protecting public beach access and coastal resources through petition and advocacy.

properties.title: California Coastal National Monument Expansion Act
properties.description: Congressional bill to designate 6,200 acres in Humboldt, Santa Cruz, and San Luis Obispo Counties under California Coastal National Monument, protecting coastal lands with historical, cultural, scientific, ecological value.

properties.title: Kauai Chapter helps end polluted discharge along West Kauai
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Kauai Chapter helps end polluted discharge along West Kauai
properties.description: Surfrider sued Hawaii's ADC for Clean Water Act violations. Court ruled ADC must obtain permits, limit pollution from 40 miles of drainage ditches discharging pesticide-laden sediment into West Kauai waters at Polihale, Kekaha beaches.

properties.title: Ban More Foam in San Francisco
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban More Foam in San Francisco
properties.description: Expanded SF's polystyrene ban to prohibit sale of foam food service ware, packing materials, beach toys, and marine equipment not encapsulated. Strictest US foam ordinance protecting ocean from plastic pollution.

properties.title: Protect NC Public Trust Rights to Beach Access
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Protect NC Public Trust Rights to Beach Access
properties.description: Defended NC's public trust doctrine ensuring dry-sand beach access in Nies v. Town of Emerald Isle case. Surfrider filed amicus brief supporting Town. NC Supreme Court upheld public beach access rights Dec 2016.

properties.title: Save the Indian River Lagoon
properties.description: 10-year $302.8M cleanup plan for Indian River Lagoon addressing algal blooms, toxic muck, leaky septic systems. Funded by sales tax. Includes muck removal, septic upgrades, fertilizer management, education, living shorelines. Approved Nov 2016.

properties.title: Protect Matunuck!
properties.description: Surfrider opposed Ocean Mist bar's seawall expansion at Matunuck Beach, RI. Hard structures cause beach loss & block surf access. Forced withdrawal of faulty maintenance permit in 2016. Advocates managed retreat over armoring.

properties.title: NY Bag Fee Prohibition
properties.description: Campaign to stop NY state legislation prohibiting local bag fees. NYC passed 5¢ single-use bag fee; state senator introduced ban. Surfrider chapters mobilized grassroots pressure, preventing Assembly vote.

properties.title: Miami-Dade Polystyrene Ban
properties.description: Ban polystyrene in Miami-Dade County parks, beaches, marinas, trails. Passed June 2016, enforced June 2017. $50-$200 fines for violations. Protects marine environments from plastic pollution.

properties.title: Enforcing the Clean Water Act on Kaua'i
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Enforcing the Clean Water Act on Kaua'i
properties.description: Legal action to stop unpermitted agricultural drainage discharges polluting west Kaua'i waters. 2019 settlement requires NPDES permit, water quality monitoring for pesticides/toxins, and public data disclosure to protect Barking Sands Beach.

properties.title: Folly Beach, SC Plastic Bag and Foam Cooler Ordinance
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Folly Beach, SC Plastic Bag and Foam Cooler Ordinance
properties.description: Ordinance banning single-use plastic bags and foam coolers/takeout wares at retail establishments to reduce ocean pollution and protect sea turtles and salt marshes at Folly Beach.

properties.title: Defending San Diego County's Bluffs - One Piece at a Time
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Defending San Diego County's Bluffs - One Piece at a Time
properties.description: Surfrider San Diego defended Encinitas bluffs from hazardous development, securing 79ft setback, no basement, and seawall waiver to protect coastline resilience against sea level rise for future generations.

properties.title: Oahu Passes Plastic Bag Ban & Fee
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Oahu Passes Plastic Bag Ban & Fee
properties.description: Surfrider led effort to close loopholes in plastic bag ban and place fee on paper/plastic bags. After 5 years, Honolulu City Council passed Bill 59 CD3 to phase out all plastic bags by 2020, reducing litter on Oahu.

properties.title: Pres. Obama Expands Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Pres. Obama Expands Papahanoumokuakea and Creates the Largest Marine Monument in the World
properties.description: Obama expanded Papahānaumokuākea from 139,800 to 639,300 sq mi in Sept 2016, creating world's largest marine protected area, protecting monk seals, green turtles, whales in Northwestern Hawaiian Islands

properties.title: Shut Down Enbridge Line 5
properties.description: Campaign to shut down 67-year-old oil pipelines crossing Straits of Mackinac. Why: prevent catastrophic oil spill threatening 700+ miles of Great Lakes coastline. What: terminate Enbridge Line 5 easement. Victory: Michigan revoked easement May 2021.

properties.title: Stop Illegal Beach Obstructions
properties.description: Campaign to remove misleading signs, ropes, chains & fences blocking public beach access in Walton County. Implemented Leave No Trace ordinance prohibiting beach obstructions, adopted June 2016.

properties.title: Help Save the Surf at Tamarack
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Help Save the Surf at Tamarack (Change sand deposits in Carlsbad)
properties.description: Monitoring sand dredge from Agua Hedionda Lagoon to protect Tamarack surf. Surfrider advocated to redirect dredged sand from over-wide North Beach to sand-starved middle/south beaches in Carlsbad, preserving surfing resources.

properties.title: New England's Canyons and Seamounts Protected
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/New England's Canyons and Seamounts Protected!
properties.description: Obama Admin created first Atlantic Marine National Monument protecting 3 canyons & 4 seamounts in Gulf of Maine from overfishing/mining, preserving biodiversity & recreation. Surfrider supported coalition effort.

properties.title: Ban the Bag in York, Maine!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban the Bag in York, Maine!
properties.description: Surfrider Foundation Maine Chapter supported Bring Your Own Bag York to pass York's single-use plastic bag ban. Voters approved the ordinance 59% on Nov 3, 2015, making York the first Maine town to ban plastic bags.

properties.title: Defeat of Prop 81 & Confirmation of Supreme Court Victory
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Defeat of Prop 81 & Confirmation of Supreme Court Victory
properties.description: Defeated Proposal 81 zoning amendment that would have allowed developers to bypass local laws in Waikiki. Protected coastal zoning after 2015 Supreme Court victory blocked high-rise condo development on beach.

properties.title: Shell Beach Access - Bluff Drive Public Access Protection
properties.description: Protected public pedestrian access along Bluff Drive to Pirates Cove Beach in Shell Beach, CA. CA Coastal Commission denied HOA appeal to lock gate, preserving 1960s easement for safe coastal access vs dangerous bluff climbing.

properties.title: Oregon Marine Debris Action Plan
properties.description: Statewide action plan with NOAA to reduce plastic pollution in Oregon's marine environment through volunteer cleanups, data collection, rapid response protocols, and policy advocacy including bag bans and plastic reduction initiatives.

properties.title: Long Beach NY Bag Legislation
properties.description: Coalition advocated for fee on plastic/paper bags in Long Beach, NY. Gathered 1000s of petition signatures, hosted screenings, rallied businesses. City Council passed bag legislation Oct 2016 to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

properties.title: Folly Beach, SC Bans Bags, Foam, and Balloons from the Beach
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Folly Beach, SC Bans Bags, Foam, and Balloons from the Beach
properties.description: Folly Beach banned plastic bags, foam containers, and balloons from the beach in 2016 to prevent marine litter and wildlife harm. Violators face $500 fine or 30 days jail. Builds on earlier retail distribution ban.

properties.title: Protect public health in Nāwiliwili Stream
properties.description: Surfrider Kaua'i posted warning signs at Kalapakī Bay where Nāwiliwili Stream discharges, alerting families to chronic high bacteria levels 4-8x state standards. Testing since 2016 shows sewage contamination from cesspools.

properties.title: Protect The Columbia River
properties.description: Surfrider opposed Tesoro Savage oil terminal on Columbia River. 279,000 comments submitted. WA Governor rejected project in 2018 citing earthquake, spill risks, and climate impacts. Victory for river and ocean protection.

properties.title: Access to Tidal Waterways Statewide in NJ
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Access to Tidal Waterways Statewide in NJ
properties.description: NJ legislation codifying Public Trust Doctrine to ensure public access to beaches and tidal lands. Bill S.1074 signed into law May 2019, protecting coastal access rights after previous rules struck down by courts.

properties.title: Stop CEMEX Sand Mining
properties.description: Campaign to halt illegal coastal sand mining by CEMEX in Marina, CA. Mining ~270k cubic yards/year caused beach erosion at Marina Dunes, Fort Ord Dunes, Monterey State Beach. Victory: CA Coastal Commission shut down operations 2017.

properties.title: World Oceans Day Resolution in Rhode Island!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/World Oceans Day Resolution in Rhode Island!
properties.description: Surfrider RI Chapter supported resolution HB6283 & S0965 to recognize June 8, 2015 as World Oceans Day, drawing statewide attention to ocean, wave & beach protection. Passed by House & Senate June 4, 2015.

properties.title: Strengthen Barrington's Bag Ordinance
properties.description: Surfrider RI urged Barrington town council to amend bag ban ordinance, closing loopholes exploited by plastics industry. Amendments passed 2016 increasing thickness definition to 4ml, reducing single-use plastic bags entering ocean.

properties.title: Surfing is Not a Crime in Pacific City, OR
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Surfing is Not a Crime in Pacific City, OR
properties.description: Defeated Oregon Marine Board proposal to restrict surfing in 1100-yard safety zone at Cape Kiwanda, Pacific City. Surfrider led grassroots campaign with 1600+ petition signatures. Board unanimously denied restriction June 2015.

properties.title: Walton County's Obstructions on the Beach Ordinance
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Walton County's Obstructions on the Beach Ordinance
properties.description: Surfrider Emerald Coast advocates for enforcement of ordinance prohibiting ropes, chains, signs on Walton County beaches. Protects public access, prevents injuries. Ordinance strengthened June 2016 after advocacy.

properties.title: Isle of Palms, SC, Enacts Plastic Bag Ban
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Isle of Palms, SC, Enacts Plastic Bag Ban
properties.description: First SC city to ban single-use plastic bags. Prohibits retailers from distributing plastic carryout bags at city facilities and businesses. Protects coastal waters from plastic pollution. Enacted June 2015, effective 6 months later.

properties.title: Ban Single-Use Plastic Bags in Oceanside
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Ban Single-Use Plastic Bags in Oceanside
properties.description: Surfrider San Diego Chapter campaigned to ban plastic shopping bags in Oceanside, CA. City Council approved ordinance in Aug 2016, requiring stores to stop using single-use plastic bags starting Jan 2017.

properties.title: No New Beach Raking on Cocoa Beach!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/No New Beach Raking on Cocoa Beach!
properties.description: Campaign stopped Cocoa Beach proposal to mechanically rake 1-mile beach section. Raking destroys wrack lines, harms sea turtle nesting habitat (2nd largest Loggerhead population), impacts dunes. Victory achieved.

properties.title: Oregon Marine Debris Prevention
properties.description: Legislative campaign establishing Submerged Land Enhancement Fund to remove derelict boats, docks & debris from Oregon inland waterways before reaching beaches. Passed July 2015, prevents disasters like Lighthouse Beach foam incident.

properties.title: Atlantic Protected from Seismic Blasting
properties.description: Campaign to stop seismic airgun blasting for oil/gas exploration off Mid- and South Atlantic coast. Victory in 2017 when BOEM denied all permits, protecting marine mammals including endangered Right Whales from noise pollution.

properties.title: Banned Plastic Bags in California
properties.description: Surfrider Foundation led coalition to uphold California's statewide plastic bag ban (SB 270/Prop 67). Voters approved ban in Nov 2016 with 54% support, addressing ocean plastic pollution at grocery stores and retailers statewide.

properties.title: Microbead-Free Waters Act
properties.description: Federal ban on plastic microbeads in personal care products. Prevents tiny plastics from facial scrubs/toothpastes entering waterways and oceans via wastewater. Phased manufacturing/sales ban 2017-2019.

properties.title: Parking & Access Preserved at Higgins Beach!
properties.description: Surfrider Maine Chapter successfully defended free public parking at Higgins Beach, Scarborough against removal proposal. Ordinance Committee voted 2-to-1 to dismiss restrictions, preserving beach access for surfers and community.

properties.title: Walton County Customary Use Ordinance
properties.description: Protect public beach access in Walton County's Emerald Coast. Ordinance recognizes customary use rights to dry sand beaches for recreation, adopted Oct 2016, effective Apr 2017. 15-foot buffer from structures/dunes.

properties.title: South Jersey - Longport, NJ Fee on Bags
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/South Jersey - Longport, NJ Fee on Bags
properties.description: Campaign to make Longport first NJ town with plastic bag ordinance. Educating merchants, showing 'Bag It' film to officials, conducting cleanups. Part of 'Downbeach' effort covering Ventnor, Margate, Longport.

properties.title: San Diego Secondary Treatment Waiver
properties.description: San Diego's wastewater treatment waiver enables Pure Water recycling project, reducing ocean discharge from Point Loma plant. Commits to 83MGD wastewater reuse by 2035 vs upgrading to secondary treatment.

properties.title: Atlantic Coast Protected from Offshore Drilling
properties.description: Campaign to stop offshore oil drilling on Atlantic Coast. Grassroots effort with 34 chapters, rallies, resolutions, thousands of comments. Successful March 2016 when BOEM canceled drilling plans for 2017-2022.

properties.title: Loam not Foam - Oregon Schools Polystyrene Ban
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Loam not Foam - Oregon Schools Polystyrene Ban
properties.description: Student-led campaign to ban polystyrene foam in Oregon schools. HB 2762 eliminates foam plates/trays from school meals to prevent marine litter. Signed into law June 16, 2015 after testimony by Sunnyside & Bandon students.

properties.title: Mitigate Plastic Marine Debris in Maine
properties.description: Maine legislation LD427 to reduce plastic marine debris & microdebris pollution. Surfrider Maine Chapter supported bill, passed House & Senate 2016. Protects ocean resources for coastal livelihoods & recreation.

properties.title: Microbeads BANNED in Connecticut!
properties.description: Connecticut banned plastic microbeads in personal care products via 2015 budget bill. Surfrider testimony closed industry loopholes. Phase-out protects marine waters from synthetic plastic pollution.

properties.title: Support the Bag Ordinance in Falmouth!
properties.description: Campaign to ban single-use plastic bags in Falmouth, Maine to reduce plastic marine debris. Ordinance passed Jan 2016 with 5-cent fee on all single-use bags, effective April 1, 2016. Led by Surfrider Maine Chapter since Oct 2014.

properties.title: Protect Access at Higgins for Everyone, for Good!
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Protect Access at Higgins for Everyone, for Good!
properties.description: Campaign to preserve public beach access at Higgins Beach, Scarborough, Maine. Fought ordinances limiting parking hours and beach use. Achieved victory maintaining 6AM parking and 1-hour limits despite parking meters installation.

properties.title: California's Trash Policy Becomes Law
properties.description: Statewide rule preventing trash from entering California waters. Requires stormwater permits to include trash provisions, reaching zero trash goal within 10 years. Targets plastic pollution in marine environment.

properties.title: City of Huntington Beach Plastic Bag Ban Repeal
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/City of Huntington Beach Plastic Bag Ban Repeal
properties.description: Campaign to keep Huntington Beach's plastic bag ban in place, preventing repeal attempt by city council members. Aimed to reduce plastic litter from beaches, streets, and rivers through reusable bag use.

properties.title: Save the Helo - Newport Coast Guard Environmental and Recreational Response
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Save the Helo - Newport Coast Guard Environmental and Recreational Response
properties.description: Campaign to retain Coast Guard helicopter in Newport, Oregon for oil spill response and ocean safety. Relocation 90 miles south would delay environmental emergency response at high-traffic port. Victory: Congress funded 12-month extension.

properties.title: Florida 2014 Balloon Release Bill
properties.description: Campaign to stop Florida Legislature from increasing helium balloon release limit from 10 to 100 balloons for funerals/memorials. Balloons pollute ocean when released, harming marine life through ingestion and entanglement.

properties.title: HI State Legislature Passes Stormwater Bill
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/HI State Legislature Passes Stormwater Bill
properties.description: Hawaii bill HB1325 allows counties to charge stormwater utility fees to reduce runoff into ocean. Surfrider Hawaii Chapters drafted bill with Rep. Chris Lee, formed coalition, educated public. Passed 4/26/15, signed into law.

properties.title: California Bans Plastic Microbeads
properties.description: Ban plastic microbeads in personal care products in California. Microbeads wash down drains, bypass wastewater treatment, and pollute waterways and ocean. AB 888 prohibits sale of products containing microbeads.

properties.title: Miami Beach Foam Ban
properties.description: Ban on EPS foam coolers and foodware in Miami Beach to reduce marine pollution. Started with beach ban, expanded citywide. Enforcement began with education, warnings, then fines by Nov 2016.

properties.title: Climate Change Adaptation Incorporated into State Budget
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Climate Change Adaptation Incorporated into State Budget
properties.description: Surfrider advocated for coastal protection resulting in $3M Climate Resilience Account for coastal agencies to address sea level rise and climate change adaptation. Signed into state budget June 2014.

properties.title: Recreational Use Characterization Proposal
properties.description: Surfrider led project mapping coastal/marine recreation in New England to fill data gaps for ocean planning. Characterizes spatial patterns of surfing, kayaking, diving, beach use to protect recreational areas in Regional Ocean Planning.

properties.title: Polystyrene Foam Ban in City of San Luis Obispo, CA
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Polystyrene Foam Ban in City of San Luis Obispo, CA
properties.description: Ban on polystyrene foam distribution and retail sale in San Luis Obispo, CA to reduce marine litter. Surfrider Foundation SLO Chapter and SLO FOAM Free coalition advocated. City Council unanimously passed ordinance June 2.

properties.title: Melbourne Beach Voluntary Bag Ban
properties.description: Voluntary plastic bag reduction program in Melbourne Beach, FL. Partnership between Surfrider's Sebastian Inlet Chapter and City Council to reduce plastic bags despite state preemption law. Modeled after St. Augustine Beach.

properties.title: Save the Spit on Sea Island, GA
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Save the Spit on Sea Island, GA
properties.description: Prevented development on fragile, eroding south tip of Sea Island, GA. Lawsuit settlement preserved 90% of spit (80+ acres) in conservation easement, funded 5-year coastal erosion study. Protects ecologically sensitive coastline.

properties.title: Encinitas EPS Foam Foodware Ordinance
properties.description: Ban on expanded polystyrene foam food service items at Encinitas restaurants, city facilities and events. Addresses top-ten beach cleanup pollutant with health concerns. Surfrider San Diego advocated through workshops and hearings.

properties.title: Town of Surfside Bag Ordinance
properties.description: Surfside, FL banned single-use plastic bags in 2019 to reduce litter, protect storm drains, and address marine pollution. Collaboration between town, businesses, activists, and Surfrider Foundation Miami Chapter.

properties.title: Oregon Lighthouse Beach Protection
properties.description: Coastal erosion threatened cliff-edge home at Lighthouse Beach, Coos Bay. Surfrider advocated managed retreat over seawalls. Victory: home relocated in 2016, protecting beach and public safety while meeting homeowner needs.

properties.title: Bag Ban Newburyport, Mass
properties.description: Surfrider Chapter supported coalition to pass plastic bag ban in Newburyport, MA to reduce marine plastic pollution. Next step: add paper bag fee to strengthen ordinance protecting coastal waters.

properties.title: Beach Access Litigation Victory in Rhode Island
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Beach Access Litigation Victory in Rhode Island
properties.description: Surfrider RI intervened in lawsuit over home built on Rose Nulman Park public land. June 2014 RI Supreme Court ruled for demolition, protecting public beach access near Point Judith Lighthouse, Narragansett.

properties.title: A Plan for Our Ocean in the Mid-Atlantic
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/A Plan for Our Ocean in the Mid-Atlantic
properties.description: Surfrider works with Mid-Atlantic Regional Planning Body to secure spatial protections for priority ecological and recreational coastal areas in NY, NJ, DE, MD, VA through comprehensive ocean management plan.

properties.title: Shoreline Master Program Updates for Pacific County
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Shoreline Master Program Updates for Pacific County
properties.description: Surfrider advocated for updated Shoreline Master Plans in Pacific County, WA to protect ecosystems, improve shoreline resiliency, ensure public access, and plan for sea level rise. Approved Jan 2018.

properties.title: Washington Marine Spatial Planning
properties.description: Completed marine spatial plan protecting fisheries & sensitive marine ecosystems off Washington coast. Baseline data, improved coordination among tribes/agencies, project requirements for ocean use proposals. Finalized June 2018.

properties.title: Shoreline Master Program Updates for Grays Harbor County
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Shoreline Master Program Updates for Grays Harbor County
properties.description: Surfrider Foundation led 7-year effort to update Grays Harbor's Shoreline Master Program, protecting 1,200+ miles of shorelines including Pacific Ocean, Grays Harbor, rivers. Approved July 2020, effective Aug 11, 2020.

properties.title: Protect Grays Harbor from Massive Oil Terminals
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Protect Grays Harbor from Massive Oil Terminals
properties.description: Campaign to stop 3 oil export terminal proposals in Grays Harbor, WA. Victory achieved Aug 2017 when Port and developers abandoned plans, protecting Chehalis watershed and coast from oil spill risks via rail/vessel traffic.

properties.title: Coastal Resilience Funding for FY 2015
properties.description: Congress allocated $5M to NOAA's regional coastal resilience program supporting ocean planning via MARCO, NROC, WCGA partnerships under National Ocean Policy for ocean/coast stewardship

properties.title: Kakaako Makai Saved—Again!
properties.description: Coalition stopped luxury high-rise development on Kakaako Makai public coastland, Honolulu's last South Shore open space. Defeated 2014 exemption bill, upholding 2006 law banning residential development.

properties.title: Clean Up Cowell's
properties.description: Campaign to remove Cowell's Beach from the dirtiest beach list through water quality improvement efforts at this Santa Cruz, California coastal location.

properties.title: Governor Includes Critical Funding for Coastal Commission
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Governor Includes Critical Funding for Coastal Commission
properties.description: Surfrider advocated for $4M funding for CA Coastal Commission to update Local Coastal Plans addressing climate change impacts, sea level rise, storms, coastal erosion and flooding threats to infrastructure and resources.

properties.title: Short Sands Water Quality Protection
properties.description: Replaced failing septic system at Short Sands beach, Oregon to reduce bacteria levels in creeks and surf spot. New drain field handles 700k+ visits/yr. Ongoing monitoring via Blue Water Task Force near Cape Falcon Marine Reserve.

properties.title: Restrict Vehicle Access near Naval Jetty in Cape Henlopen State Park
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Restrict Vehicle Access near Naval Jetty in Cape Henlopen State Park
properties.description: Campaign to exclude vehicles from beach area near Naval Jetty at Cape Henlopen State Park, Delaware. Addresses fake fishing to avoid walking, protects surfing/swimming areas. State created vehicle-free safety zone in 2014.

properties.title: Protect Oregon's Marine Reserves
properties.description: Advocacy for Oregon's Marine Reserve Program at Cape Perpetua, Cascade Head, Cape Falcon, Otter Rock & Redfish Rocks. Supporting funding, monitoring, community engagement & climate resilience since 2012.

properties.title: Stop the Port Ambrose LNG Facility
properties.description: Campaign to stop offshore LNG facility 17 miles off Jones Beach, NY. Opposed seafloor dredging, pipeline installation, and fracked gas export infrastructure threatening marine ecosystems and coastal waters. Vetoed November 2015.

properties.title: Morro Bay Water Resources Center Moved Off The Coast
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Morro Bay Water Resources Center Moved Off The Coast
properties.description: Relocated wastewater treatment plant inland in 2022, first in California to move off coast. Reduces waste release risk from floods, tsunamis, sea level rise. Upgrades treatment, produces recycled water.

properties.title: Los Angeles County Bag Ban Defense in Court
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Los Angeles County Bag Ban Defense in Court
properties.description: Surfrider filed amicus brief supporting LA County's bag ban ordinance against plastics industry challenge. Court ruled Feb 2013 that paper bag charges aren't taxes under Prop 26. Protects ocean from plastic pollution.

properties.title: Washington Campaign for Ocean Planning Fund
properties.description: Ocean planning in Washington to identify sensitive coastal resources and popular activities, then plan new uses while minimizing impacts to marine life, recreation, and human uses on the Pacific coast.

properties.title: Open Martin's Beach - Coastal Act Litigation
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Open Martin's Beach - Coastal Act Litigation
properties.description: Restore public access to Martin's Beach near Half Moon Bay, closed in 2008. Surfrider won lawsuit under CA Coastal Act requiring beach remain open unless owner obtains permit. Protects generations of family beach access.

properties.title: Solana Beach Seawall Policy Defended
properties.description: 16-year campaign to manage seawalls protecting beach access and coastal health. Established 20-year permit reviews, mitigation fees for beach loss, and restrictions on armoring for accessory structures. Won in CA Court 2018.

properties.title: Defeated Pismo Beach Seawall
properties.description: Surfrider opposed seawalls at two Pismo Beach lift stations. Coastal Commission denied 2011 proposal, conditionally approved 2013 sculpted seawall requiring relocation plan within 5 years instead of permanent armoring.

properties.title: NYC Bag Fee Legislation
properties.description: 5-cent fee on single-use bags to reduce 9 billion plastic bags used yearly in NYC. Coalition campaign with BagitNYC, passed after 2 years. Merchant keeps fee. Modeled after successful DC program.

properties.title: Oppose West Basin Desalination Plant
properties.description: Campaign opposing ocean desalination plant in LA's West Basin. Advocated for recycled water & conservation instead. Project terminated Dec 2021 after 20yr fight, protecting coast from brine discharge & marine life impacts.

properties.title: University of Hawaii Bans EPS Foam on Campus
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/University of Hawaii Bans EPS Foam on Campus
properties.description: UH Manoa banned EPS foam at dining locations through student petition and collaboration with administration. Policy encourages reusable/compostable products, bans foam for vendors. Approved April 2013.

properties.title: Northeast Regional Ocean Planning
properties.description: Surfrider advocates for holistic ocean management in New England. Successfully influenced 2016 Northeast Regional Ocean Plan certification. Focuses on protecting coastal ecosystems and recreation areas through stakeholder engagement.

properties.title: Ruggles is Saved!
properties.description: Protected Ruggles Ave surf break in Newport, RI from jetty construction during Cliff Walk repairs post-Hurricane Sandy. Community advocacy led to approval of surfer-friendly, lower-impact repair plans in July 2013.

properties.title: Sea Breeze Estates Illegal Retaining Wall, Dune Destruction
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Sea Breeze Estates Illegal Retaining Wall, Dune Destruction
properties.description: Fought removal of illegal 12-14' retaining wall at Sea Breeze Estates, South Padre Island, TX. Wall violated 200' setback rule, threatened public beach access & dunes. Victory: wall removed, developer fined $429k, dune mitigation ordered.

properties.title: Surfrider's Hawaii Chapters Help Repeal the PLDC
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Surfrider's Hawaii Chapters Help Repeal the PLDC!
properties.description: Hawaii Surfrider chapters led grassroots coalition to repeal Public Lands Development Corporation, preventing private development of public lands, harbors and coastal areas. Successful campaign ended April 22, 2013.

properties.title: Bag Fee in Portland, Maine
properties.description: Surfrider Maine Chapter helped pass 5-cent fee on checkout bags in Portland. Worked with City Council's Green Packaging Working Group. Ordinance effective April 2015 to reduce plastic pollution in ocean and beaches.

properties.title: Culver City Plastic Bag Ban
properties.description: Ban plastic bags & 10¢ paper bag fee at grocery/food retailers. Approved unanimously May 2013, effective Nov 2013. Based on LA County model. Protects coastal waters from plastic pollution.

properties.title: Fruitstands Public Beach Access Restored
properties.description: Surfrider Ventura County restored public access to Fruitstands surf break near McGrath State Beach, Oxnard CA, blocked by oil company fencing in 2012. Coastal Commission violation notice led to access restoration in 2014.

properties.title: Stopped Expansion of Rock Revetment in Dana Point
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Stopped Expansion of Rock Revetment in Dana Point
properties.description: Stopped Orange County's proposal to rebuild/expand 1300ft rock revetment at Niguel Shores that would impact shoreline processes, sand supply & beach access. No mitigation offered by county/homeowners. Dana Point, CA.

properties.title: Rincón, PR Plastic Bag Ban
properties.description: Rincón became first Puerto Rico municipality to ban single-use checkout bags in 2014. Surfrider activists drafted ordinance with local government and sewed reusable bags from donated fabric to provide alternatives.

properties.title: Progressive Stormwater Permit for San Diego Region
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Progressive Stormwater Permit for San Diego Region
properties.description: San Diego Regional Water Board approved watershed-based MS4 stormwater permit in 2013, rejecting safe harbor clause. Uses Low Impact Development to reduce ocean pollution from contaminated stormwater runoff.

properties.title: Seismic Testing on Central CA Coast Stopped
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Seismic Testing on Central CA Coast Stopped
properties.description: California Coastal Commission denied PG&E's seismic testing near Diablo Canyon Nuclear Plant. 400+ opposed due to marine harm vs marginal earthquake hazard benefits. Coalition of environmental groups succeeded.

properties.title: City of Miami Beach Single Use Plastic Straw Ordinance
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/City of Miami Beach Single Use Plastic Straw Ordinance
properties.description: Ordinance banning single-use plastic straws citywide in Miami Beach to prevent marine pollution. Passed Sept 2019 after 7 years of advocacy. Complements existing beach property restrictions.

properties.title: Defeated Bad Coastal Act Legislation in CA
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Defeated Bad Coastal Act Legislation in CA
properties.description: Surfrider defeated AB 2211 that would have gutted California's Coastal Act protections. Partnered with organizations, lobbied Sacramento, testified at hearing. Bill killed 6-3 vote on May 7, preserving coastal development standards.

properties.title: Singer Island Groin Proposal
properties.description: Proposed erosion control project for 1 mile of Singer Island coastline using groins/T-groins to trap sediment and allow beach sand accretion. Project rejected Feb 2012 due to cost and effectiveness concerns.

properties.title: First Coast Chapter Beach Access Restrictions
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/First Coast Chapter Beach Access Restrictions
properties.description: Campaign to restore beach park hours at Huguenot Memorial Park and Hanna Park in Jacksonville after budget cuts reduced access from 8pm to 6pm. City Council voted April 18th to restore summer hours starting April 28th.

properties.title: San Luis Obispo County Bag Ban
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/San Luis Obispo County Bag Ban
properties.description: Surfrider SLO Chapter supported countywide ordinance banning single-use plastic bags and adding 10¢ paper bag fee to reduce waste and prevent plastic marine pollution. Passed Jan 2012 after 6-year process.

properties.title: Jenness Beach Parking Victory
properties.description: Surfrider opposed permit-parking restrictions at Jenness Beach, Rye NH. Advocated for public beach access via signs & outreach. Residents voted down Articles 18 & 19 in March election, preserving non-resident parking.

properties.title: Sanctuary Expansion in Northern California
properties.description: Expanded Gulf of Farallones & Cordell Bank sanctuaries by 2,800 sq mi to Point Arena, protecting marine ecosystems from oil/gas drilling. Supports fisheries, recreation, tourism along Northern California coast.

properties.title: Hermosa Beach Bag Ban
properties.description: Ban single-use plastic bags at retail establishments in Hermosa Beach to reduce marine plastic pollution. City Council passed 4-0 vote on Aug 25, requiring recyclable paper or reusable bags at checkout.

properties.title: Seismic Testing Defeated on the Atlantic Coast
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Seismic Testing Defeated on the Atlantic Coast
properties.description: Surfrider and coalition partners successfully halted seismic airgun testing for oil/gas exploration off Mid- and South Atlantic coast, protecting 130,000+ marine mammals from injury and disruption to feeding, mating, migration.

properties.title: Rewild Surfers Point
properties.description: Managed retreat project in Ventura, CA relocating eroding bike path and parking lot inland, restoring shoreline with cobble berm, sand dunes, and native vegetation. Nature-based solution preventing seawalls, enhancing resilience.

properties.title: Marine Debris Reauthorization Act
properties.description: Federal law reauthorizing NOAA's Marine Debris Program to identify, assess, prevent, reduce marine debris impacts on US economy, marine environment, navigation. Signed Dec 2012, addresses plastic ocean pollution nationally.

properties.title: City of Santa Cruz Expanded EPS Foam Ban
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/City of Santa Cruz Expanded EPS Foam Ban
properties.description: Santa Cruz banned EPS foam products at retail/restaurants to prevent ocean pollution. Surfrider activists supported via petitions and council testimony. Prohibits foam cups, coolers, toys, packaging citywide since July 2012.

properties.title: City of Los Angeles Plastic Bag Ban
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/City of Los Angeles Plastic Bag Ban
properties.description: LA County banned single-use plastic bags at supermarkets/pharmacies in unincorporated areas, affecting 1M+ people. 10 cent fee on paper bags. Largest municipal ban to date. Protects coastal waters from plastic pollution.

properties.title: Wrightsville Beach NC Smoking Ban
properties.description: Cape Fear Chapter campaigned for beach smoking ban to reduce cigarette butt pollution. After 2 years, passed as ballot initiative. One family collected 35,000 butts in a year as part of 'Hold On To Your Butt' campaign.

properties.title: Settlement Protects Coastal Waters from Harms of Oil Spill Dispersants
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Settlement Protects Coastal Waters from Harms of Oil Spill Dispersants
properties.description: Legal settlement requiring EPA and Coast Guard to consult marine experts before approving toxic oil dispersants, preventing harm to sea life and coastal resources after incidents like Deepwater Horizon.

properties.title: Save Cherry Point
properties.description: Coalition effort led by Lummi Nation defeated proposed coal export terminal at Cherry Point, Bellingham. Protected sacred waters, world-class recreation from environmental damage. US Army Corps denied permits May 2016.

properties.title: San Elijo Lagoon Restoration Project
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/San Elijo Lagoon Restoration Project incorporates surf monitoring
properties.description: Lagoon restoration in San Diego SMCA to improve circulation, water quality & biological productivity. Includes 12-month surf monitoring to track dredging/sediment impacts on nearby waves. Addresses sea level rise & flooding.

properties.title: Ban the Bag in Brigantine
properties.description: Campaign to ban single-use plastic bags in Brigantine, NJ. Surfrider South Jersey Chapter collected postcards, advocated for legislation. Town introduced plastic bag ban ordinance August 15, 2018 after years of activism.

properties.title: Solana Beach Bag Ban
properties.description: Solana Beach became first San Diego County city to ban single-use plastic bags in April 2012. Unanimous city council vote advanced ocean conservation by preventing plastic pollution from reaching coastal waters.

properties.title: Huntington Beach Reusable Bag Ordinance
properties.description: Surfrider Foundation worked with Huntington Beach to ban plastic checkout bags and add 10¢ paper bag fee. Reduces ocean plastic pollution, protects wildlife, prevents drain clogging. Effective Nov 1, 2013.

properties.title: Carpinteria CA - Bag Ban
properties.description: Carpinteria banned single-use plastic/paper bags at retailers to reduce marine pollution. Surfrider Foundation Santa Barbara Chapter campaigned for this ordinance, approved March 12, 2012, making it CA's first South Coast city with such ban.

properties.title: Laguna Beach Plastic Bag Ban
properties.description: Ban on single-use plastic bags at Laguna Beach stores/facilities to reduce ocean pollution. Grocery stores/pharmacies may offer recycled paper bags for fee. Approved Feb 2012 with 6-month transition period.

properties.title: Hilo Chapter Helps Pass Bill to Open Access to Papaikou Mill Beach
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Hilo Chapter Helps Pass Bill to Open Access to Papaikou Mill Beach
properties.description: Surfrider's Hilo Chapter fought to restore public access to Papaikou Mill Beach after owners limited trail use. County passed Resolution 308-12 in Nov 2012 authorizing eminent domain of historic beach trail for surfing, fishing, education.

properties.title: State Supreme Court Victory in the Kyo-Ya Case
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/State Supreme Court Victory in the Kyo-Ya Case
properties.description: Hawaii Supreme Court blocked Kyo-Ya Resort's 26-story hotel expansion into Waikiki Beach setback area. 5-year campaign by Surfrider & allies protected coastal setback laws, preventing 60-foot encroachment on Hawaii's most popular beach.

properties.title: Stop Pollution of the Lahaina Wastewater Injection Wells
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Stop Pollution of the Lahaina Wastewater Injection Wells
properties.description: Lawsuit won to stop Maui County from injecting 3-5M gallons daily of treated sewage into groundwater that seeps into ocean, harming marine life and coral reefs. County must divert wastewater, fund reuse projects, obtain permits.

properties.title: Attempt to Delay Implementation of 2008 Ocean Outfall Legislation Fails
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Attempt to Delay Implementation of 2008 Ocean Outfall Legislation Fails
properties.description: 2008 FL legislation to close 6 ocean outfalls along Atlantic coast by 2025 to preserve reef ecosystem & reuse freshwater. 2011 bill attempting to extend deadline failed, keeping original timeline intact.

properties.title: Barrington RI Plastic Bag Ban
properties.description: First RI city to ban plastic checkout bags at stores/restaurants. Surfrider RI Chapter advocated through support letters and public meetings. Optional 5-cent paper bag fee encourages reusable bags. Adopted Oct 2012.

properties.title: Nueces County Erosion Response Plan
properties.description: Erosion Response Plan for Corpus Christi/Nueces County establishing 350ft coastal setback, protecting dune systems (14ft high, 50% vegetation), ensuring 100ft public beach access. Passed 2012 after advocacy by Surfrider Texas Coastal Bend Chapter.

properties.title: Destin Customary Use Legal Access Case
properties.description: Legal case defending public beach access rights in Destin/South Walton County, FL. Homeowners challenged customary use doctrine. Surfrider filed Amicus Brief. Court dismissed homeowners' claims in 2012, upholding public access.

properties.title: Surfrider's Oahu Chapter Helps Pass Smoking Ban
properties.url: https://www.surfrider.org/campaigns/Surfrider's Oahu Chapter Helps Pass Smoking Ban!
properties.description: Oahu Chapter lobbied for island-wide smoking ban in parks and beaches. Started with South Shore ban (Bill 72, 2013), expanded to all Oahu beaches/parks (Bill 25, July 2013). Reduces pollution, protects marine life.

properties.title: RESTORE Act Passes
properties.description: Dedicates 80% of Deepwater Horizon fines to Gulf Coast Restoration Trust Fund. Restores beaches, coastal marshes, barrier islands, wildlife damaged by BP oil spill. Supports economic development, tourism, recreation, commercial fishing.
properties.funder: Clean Water Act fines from Deepwater Horizon oil spill

properties.title: Long Beach Polystyrene Ordinance
properties.description: Ban on polystyrene plastic citywide in Long Beach, CA. Prohibits EPS foam containers, rigid polystyrene, and foam coolers. Phased implementation over 18 months starting May 2018 to reduce marine plastic pollution.

properties.title: Defeated Pismo Beach/Shell Beach Seawalls
properties.description: Surfrider's San Luis Obispo Chapter successfully opposed two proposed seawalls in Pismo Beach that threatened public beach access. Through surveys, documentation, and advocacy, the California Coastal Commission denied the project in 2011.

properties.title: San Clemente Expanded Polystyrene Ban
properties.description: San Clemente, CA banned expanded polystyrene (EPS) in food service ware citywide. Approved unanimously by City Council to reduce marine plastic pollution from foam containers entering coastal waters.

properties.title: City of Monterey Bag Ban
properties.description: Ordinance to ban single-use plastic/paper bags by retailers in Monterey, with fees on recycled bags. Aims to reduce plastic marine pollution. Supported by Surfrider Monterey Chapter in 2011.

properties.title: Newport Ban the Bag
properties.description: Newport, OR banned single-use plastic bags in 2019 after Surfrider Chapter and Sam Case Elementary students advocated to City Council. Ordinance requires retailers to charge for paper/reusable bags, phased implementation by business size.

properties.title: Capitola Plastic Bag Ban
